name: Taiwanese Hokkien (Taigi)
variant: Taiwanese Hokkien of Taiwan, the mainstream mixed (general) accent that leans to Kaohsiung / Tainan and is the main reading of the Ministry of Education's 臺灣台語常用詞辭典; written in the MOE recommended characters with Tâi-lô romanisation
script: Chinese characters (traditional; the Taiwan MOE recommended characters for Taiwanese, including Taigi-only ones such as 毋, 佇, 遮, 欲, 予) with a Tâi-lô line in Latin letters with tone marks (a á à ah â ā a̍h, -- before a neutral-tone syllable); the Tâi-lô line is what the learner actually reads; left to right
basis: National Taiwan University, Basic Taiwanese for international students (PTCSL7915, 2015): pronunciation items week by week beside 生活臺語 lessons 1-8 (classroom language, self-introduction, address and phone numbers, introducing others, quantities and measure words, buying stationery, asking directions, dates), then the food topics of the follow-on NTU Intermediate Taiwanese (生活臺語 lessons 13-16: market, meat, rice and eggs, eating noodles, eating out)
src: National Taiwan University, 國際生初級臺語 Basic Taiwanese (PTCSL7915), syllabus for semester 104-1 (nol2.aca.ntu.edu.tw, syllabus_1041146U9150.pdf): 18-week schedule of pronunciation items and 生活臺語 lessons 1-8

National Taiwan University, 國際生進階臺語 Intermediate Taiwanese, syllabus for semester 104-1 (syllabus_1041146U9230.pdf): pronunciation review (sandhi groups, neutral tone, re-sandhi and sandhi before -á) and 生活臺語 lessons 9-16

National Tsing Hua University, 初級台語二 Taiwanese Basic II (11220CLC 100802 and 11310CLC 100802) syllabi: Tâi-lô initials, finals, tones, then tone sandhi (連音變化) and literary / colloquial readings (文白異讀), with dialogues on meeting, self-introduction, night market, shopping, directions, phone numbers, birthdays, transport
MOE 教育部臺灣台語常用詞辭典 (sutian.moe.edu.tw), entries 食菜 and 菜單, read for spelling (bē for 'will not' in the 食菜 example sentence, romanisation only)
Wiktionary, 未: Hokkien readings bē / bōe (POJ; Tâi-lô buē) by accent
Voice check: Microsoft Learn, Azure Speech language support (speech-to-text tables: only zh-TW Taiwanese Mandarin, no nan; the text-to-speech table did not render)
Voice check: Google Cloud Gemini-TTS supported languages (cmn-CN and cmn-tw Mandarin only, no nan); Google Cloud voice list read to about 200,000 of 534,000 characters, no nan seen
Voice check: Apple VoiceOver supported languages (Chinese: Cantonese, China mainland, Taiwan; no Hokkien)

Voice check: App Store listing of 台語AI TTS by Taigi AI Labs (standalone app, 20 uses a day free, Han characters or POJ input, no API stated); PTS and Newtalk news of 14 Jan 2026 on the MOE 臺灣台語輸入法 app (speech-to-text input only, not text-to-speech); UDN on the MOE 臺灣台語語料庫 release (corpus, audio and AI models to download, no TTS service)
note: Order: the topic order of stages 2-3 follows the NTU Basic Taiwanese schedule (生活臺語 lessons 1-8) and stage 4 takes its food topics from the NTU Intermediate schedule; 生活臺語 itself was not opened, only its lesson topics as named in the syllabi. NTU gives topics and pronunciation items, not grammar, and it assumes students already know about 450 words of Mandarin and read characters; this course does not, so the character lesson starts from zero and Tâi-lô carries the reading. All grammar lessons (是 / 毋是, 有 / 無, classifiers, 欲, 佇, 會 / 袂, the four negatives, 咧 / 矣 / 過, comparison), the split into 27 lessons and the placing of sandhi early (NTU spreads it over the semester) are my own judgment. Sound lessons: five (consonants, finals, the seven tones, and two on sandhi), because sandhi changes nearly every syllable but the last of a phrase and must be known before the first sentences. Sandhi rule taught: the southern / general circle 2→1, 1→7, 7→3, 3→2, and 5→7 (northern speakers say 5→3); checked syllables, the change before 仔 -á and the neutral tone (written --) are in the second sandhi lesson. Tâi-lô not POJ (my own knowledge, not from a source opened): Tâi-lô is the MOE's official romanisation since 2006, used by the MOE dictionary, school materials and the NTU / NTHU courses above, so learners can look up every word; POJ (Pe̍h-ōe-jī, the older church romanisation) is close: same tone marks, mainly ts / tsh for POJ ch / chh, oo for o͘, ua / ue for oa / oe, ing / ik for eng / ek, nn for ⁿ; a POJ reader can follow Tâi-lô after a page of notes. Literary and colloquial readings: taught at beginner level only where unavoidable: the two number sets (colloquial tsi̍t, nn̄g, sann for counting; literary it, jī, sam for phone numbers, addresses, 禮拜一 lé-pài-it) and surnames, which are mostly literary (林 Lîm, 陳 Tân, 王 Ông). Learner: US adults, often heritage learners who heard Taigi from parents or grandparents, so family words, greetings like 食飽未？ and politeness come early. Spelling: the Tâi-lô in titles is from my own knowledge and only a few words were checked in the MOE dictionary; course writers must check every word there. Words whose reading differs by accent (未 buē / bē, 買, 月, 過, 魚, 偌濟, 姓) are given in characters only in titles; writers should use the dictionary's main reading. Voice: no Taiwanese Hokkien text-to-speech voice was found that the app can use: none in Azure's speech-to-text tables (its TTS table did not render), none in Google's Gemini-TTS list or the part of the Cloud voice list read, none in Apple's VoiceOver list; Android voices were not checked. Search results list Taiwanese research systems and an open-source toolkit from 意傳 (not opened), and there is one standalone app (台語AI TTS, Taigi AI Labs) with no stated API or licence, and the MOE has released a speech corpus and models, not a service. So the course is text-only like Cebuano unless the lead records clips or licenses a Taiwanese engine. nan-TW is kept as the tag; the app must never fall back to a zh-TW / cmn-TW voice, which would read the characters in Mandarin.
hardest: Seven tones in citation and tone sandhi: nearly every syllable but the last of a phrase is said in a different tone from its dictionary form
Sounds English lacks: nasal vowels (-nn), the stop endings -p -t -k -h, voiced b / g / j, and aspiration (p / ph, t / th, k / kh, ts / tsh) that changes meaning
Two readings for many characters: colloquial tsi̍t, nn̄g, sann against literary it, jī, sam
Four words for 'not' (毋 m̄, 無 bô, 袂 bē, 莫 mài), and characters that differ from Mandarin's (毋, 佇, 遮, 欲)

items: nan-initials
Tâi-lô consonants: p / ph, t / th, k / kh, ts / tsh, and the voiced b, g, j
nan-finals
Vowels and endings: o against oo, nasal vowels with -nn, -m -n -ng and the stop endings -p -t -k -h
nan-tones
The seven tones and their marks: a, á, à, ah, â, ā, a̍h
nan-sandhi
Tone sandhi 1: every syllable but the last changes (2→1, 1→7, 7→3, 3→2, 5→7)
nan-sandhi-2
Tone sandhi 2: syllables ending in -p -t -k -h, before 仔 á, and the neutral tone after --
nan-greetings
Greetings: 你好 lí hó, 食飽未？, 多謝 to-siā, 歹勢 pháinn-sè, 再會 tsài-huē
nan-characters
Reading Taigi characters from zero: strokes, and words only Taigi writes (毋 m̄, 佇 tī, 遮 tsia, 欲 beh, 予 hōo)
nan-classroom
Classroom phrases: 請閣講一擺 tshiánn koh kóng tsi̍t-pái, 我聽無 guá thiann-bô, 按怎講？ án-tsuánn kóng?
nan-si
是 sī and 毋是 m̄-sī; pronouns 我 guá, 你 lí, 伊 i, and two words for 'we': 阮 guán and 咱 lán
nan-intro
Introducing yourself: 你叫啥物名？ lí kiò siánn-mih miâ?, 我是美國人 guá sī Bí-kok-lâng, 我姓林 (Lîm)
nan-questions
Question words: 啥物 siánn-mih, 啥人 siánn-lâng, 佗位 tó-uī, 當時 tang-sî, 按怎 án-tsuánn
nan-numbers
Two sets of numbers: tsi̍t, nn̄g, sann for counting; it, jī, sam and 空 khòng for phone numbers and addresses
nan-family
Introducing others and family: 阿爸 a-pah, 阿母 a-bú, 阿公 a-kong, 阿媽 a-má, 阿兄 a-hiann, 小弟 sió-tī
nan-u-bo
有 ū / 無 bô: have and there is; yes/no questions with …無？ and 敢 kám
nan-classifiers
Classifiers: 一個 tsi̍t ê, 兩本冊 nn̄g pún tsheh; 這 tsit and 彼 hit
nan-prices
Money and prices: 偌濟錢？, 箍 khoo, 傷貴 siunn kuì
nan-want
Want and need: 欲 beh, 愛 ài, 想欲 siūnn-beh
nan-place
Where things are: 佇 tī, 遮 tsia and 遐 hia, 頂懸 tíng-kuân, 下跤 ē-kha
nan-directions
Directions: 正手 tsiànn-tshiú, 倒手 tò-tshiú, 直直行 ti̍t-ti̍t kiânn, 斡 uat
nan-go-come
Going and coming: 去 khì, 來 lâi, 坐車 tsē tshia, 坐捷運 tsē tsia̍t-ūn
nan-time
Clock time and dates: 幾點？ kuí tiám?, 禮拜一 lé-pài-it, 幾月幾號？
nan-food
Ordering food at the night market: 頭家 thâu-ke, 一碗麵 tsi̍t uánn mī, 好食 hó-tsia̍h
nan-market
At the market: 菜 tshài, 肉 bah, 卵 nn̄g, 魚, and asking how much
nan-describing
Describing and comparing: 真 tsin, 誠 tsiânn, 足 tsiok; 比 pí … 較 khah, 上 siōng
nan-can
Can and may: 會 ē / 袂 bē, 會使 ē-sái, 會曉 ē-hiáu
nan-negation
Four words for 'not': 毋 m̄, 無 bô, 袂 bē, 莫 mài
nan-aspect
Actions in time: 咧 leh (in progress), 矣 ah (done), 有…過 (ever)
